final_text:
Based on the workspace logs, wire capture, and partner agreement, here is the diagnosis of the root cause:

1. **What is failing and why:**
   In the transmitted file `/outbound-wire/INV49387.edi`, the `UNB` segment is:
   `UNB+UNOA:3+TIDEWELL16:ZZZ+CORRANDALE49:ZZZ+261030:0733+674946++++++1'`
   Here, data element `UNB.0035` (Test indicator, position 11) is set to `1` (indicating a test interchange).
   According to Section 5 of the Partner Agreement with Corrandale Truck Plant (`/partners/corrandale/agreement.txt`), `UNB 0035` must be set to `1` in test interchanges only, and Corrandale's production gateway (`O0013CORRANDALE6539`) accepts production interchanges only. Because the production interchange is flagged as a test, Corrandale's gateway refuses the file at the end of transmission (`EFNA` with reason `99`: `TRANSMISSION ERROR - PLEASE RETRANSMIT`).

2. **Why the other possibilities mentioned by Corrandale are not the root cause:**
   - **OFTP2 session parameters (Buffer size and Credit):** While Tidewell's gateway sends `SSIDSDEB=16384` and `SSIDCRED=128` in `SSID`, RFC 5024 §5.3.2 specifies that these parameters are negotiated down to the smaller value returned by the Responder (`04096` and `064`), and the session and data transfer proceed normally.
   - **TLS Certificate:** Tidewell's TLS certificate (`CN=oftp.tidewell.example`) does not expire until 4 November 2026; TLS 1.3 handshakes succeed in all sessions.

3. **Who must fix it and what to change:**
   Tidewell Seating Components (the **sender**) must fix the translator/envelope configuration introduced during the 14 October EDI suite migration so that `UNB.0035` is omitted for production interchanges, truncating the trailing empty conditional elements in `UNB`.

```json
{
  "cause": "test_indicator_mismatch",
  "layer": "envelope",
  "owner": "sender",
  "location": ["UNB.0035"],
  "next_check": "none",
  "value": "UNB+UNOA:3+TIDEWELL16:ZZZ+CORRANDALE49:ZZZ+261030:0733+674946'"
}
```

# Ticket R1 (agentic)

You work on the EDI support desk that serves the sender of the file described
below. A customer has raised the ticket that follows. Everything you need to
diagnose it is in the support workspace, which you can explore only with the
tools list_dir, read_file and search (start with /README.txt). The workspace
also holds unrelated material. All companies, identifiers and documents are
synthetic. You may use at most 25 tool calls; then give your final answer.

## The ticket

```text
From: Chris Brandt, EDI desk, Tidewell Seating Components
Subject: TRANSMISSION ERROR on every invoice to Corrandale Truck Plant

Since 15 October every invoice we send to Corrandale Truck Plant is refused with 'TRANSMISSION ERROR - PLEASE RETRANSMIT'. We retransmitted invoice INV49387 twice this morning with the same result, and one connection attempt timed out. Corrandale Truck Plant say our OFTP2 set-up or our certificate is faulty. Our network team says the link is fine. On 14 October we moved to a new release of our EDI suite (OFTP2 gateway and translator); IT tells me the configuration and the maps were migrated unchanged. Please find the root cause and tell us who has to fix it.
```

## What to return

Diagnose the single root cause of this ticket. Reply in any form you like,
but end your reply with exactly one fenced ```json block holding an object
with these six keys. Only the last ```json block in your reply is graded.
Give one value per key: a key that holds several options, or a list of
alternatives, scores zero for that key.

cause: exactly one of
  authentication_failure: The OFTP2 session could not be established because a password, identification code or secure authentication check failed.
  certificate_problem: A TLS or file-security certificate is expired, untrusted or not the one in the agreement.
  character_set_violation: The interchange contains characters outside the agreed syntax identifier's character repertoire.
  compression_not_agreed: A file was sent compressed (or uncompressed) contrary to what the receiver accepts.
  duplicate_interchange: An interchange was rejected because its interchange control reference was already received from this sender.
  duplicate_virtual_file: A virtual file was refused because a virtual file with the same identification was already delivered.
  end_to_end_response_not_returned: The file was delivered but the final recipient never returned the end-to-end response.
  envelope_element_format_invalid: A UNB or UNZ data element has a value whose format or length the syntax version declared in UNB S001 does not allow.
  file_too_large: The file exceeds a size limit of the receiver.
  idoc_awaiting_processing: Inbound IDocs were created in the receiver's SAP system but were not passed to the application, because the scheduled processing that should pick them up did not run.
  idoc_mapping_error: The receiver's EDI converter mapped a correct interchange to an incorrect IDoc.
  interchange_control_count_mismatch: The interchange control count in UNZ does not match the number of messages in the interchange.
  interchange_control_reference_mismatch: The interchange control reference in UNB and in UNZ are not identical.
  intermediary_fault: A clearing centre or other intermediate location lost, altered or misrouted the file.
  invalid_destination: The OFTP2 destination of the virtual file is not known to the receiver.
  no_sender_side_fault: Nothing the sender transmitted or configured is wrong, the fault lies with the receiver, and no more specific cause in this list applies.
  not_yet_determinable: The documents fit more than one root cause equally well, so the root cause cannot be named until a further check is made.
  receiver_partner_setup_missing: The receiver has not set up the sender as agreed (EDI converter partner mapping or SAP partner profile).
  recipient_identification_mismatch: The interchange recipient identification or its qualifier in UNB is not the one in the partner agreement.
  restart_position_invalid: A restarted transfer used a restart position that is wrong, or resumed from a position other than the one the receiver confirmed.
  sap_master_data_error: Posting in the receiver's SAP system failed because of its master data (material, vendor, purchase order).
  sender_identification_mismatch: The interchange sender identification or its qualifier in UNB is not the one in the partner agreement.
  session_parameters_not_negotiated: The sender used an OFTP2 session parameter (credit, buffer size or similar) outside what was negotiated.
  syntax_identifier_not_agreed: UNB S001 declares a syntax identifier or syntax version other than the agreed one.
  test_indicator_mismatch: The interchange is flagged as test (or production) contrary to the agreement.

layer: exactly one of
  transport: The OFTP2 session or file transfer, including any intermediate location.
  envelope: The EDIFACT interchange envelope (UNB to UNZ), wherever the receiver checks it (gateway or translator).
  application: The business application side, on either party: an EDI converter or SAP IDoc processing.
  none: Only with cause no_sender_side_fault: the fault is on the receiver's side, outside the layers above.
  undetermined: Only with cause not_yet_determinable.

owner: exactly one of (who must act to fix the root cause)
  sender: The party that sent the file and raised the ticket must fix it.
  receiver: The trading partner the file is addressed to must fix it.
  intermediary: A clearing centre or other intermediate location between the parties must fix it.
  agreement: The partner agreement itself is wrong or inconsistent and must be amended before either side can fix the fault.
  undetermined: Only with cause not_yet_determinable.

location: a JSON array of strings.
List the OFTP2 fields, EDIFACT data elements or application objects, on whichever
side, whose values or settings must be changed to fix the root cause, and no
others. If the fault is a conflict between two values that must agree, list both.
Write each one as:
  OFTP2 field:                 COMMAND.FIELD, e.g. "SSID.SSIDCODE"
  EDIFACT simple data element: SEGMENT.ELEMENT, e.g. "UNH.0062"
  EDIFACT component element:   SEGMENT.COMPOSITE.COMPONENT, e.g. "UNB.S003.0010"
  Application-side object:     APP.<OBJECT>, one of CONVERTER_PARTNER_TABLE, CONVERTER_MAPPING, PARTNER_PROFILE, PROCESS_CODE, BACKGROUND_JOB, MASTER_DATA, PORT
  None of the above must change: "NONE" on its own.
  Root cause not yet determinable: "UNDETERMINED" on its own.

next_check: exactly one of (the single check that would decide the root cause if the documents do not; "none" if they do)
  none: The documents already determine the root cause.
  request_receiver_gateway_log: Ask the receiver for its OFTP2 gateway log covering the file in question.
  request_receiver_translator_log: Ask the receiver for its translator's validation log for the interchange.
  request_transmitted_copy: Obtain the file exactly as the sender's gateway transmitted it, not the archived copy.
  request_other_gateway_node_trace: Obtain the trace from the sender's other gateway node or nodes.
  request_agreement_in_force: Obtain the signed version of the partner agreement currently in force.
  request_clearing_centre_trace: Ask the clearing centre for its trace of the file.
  check_sender_clock: Check the sender gateway's system clock.
  check_certificates: Check the TLS and file-security certificates on both sides.
  resend_unchanged: Send the same file again unchanged.
  resend_with_new_identity: Send the file again as a new virtual file.

value: a JSON string holding the UNB segment exactly as the sender should transmit it for this interchange, from "UNB" up to and including its segment terminator.

Example of the format only (not a hint):
```json
{"cause": "file_too_large", "layer": "transport", "owner": "receiver", "location": ["SFID.SFIDFSIZ"], "next_check": "none", "value": "12345"}
```

1: UN/EDIFACT syntax version 3: service segment and code list extracts.
2: Prepared for this eval from the sources listed at the end. Segment layouts are
3: restated in a compact form; code values and their names are quoted exactly.
4: 
5: Provenance by part:
6:   Parts 1 to 4 (syntax rules: UNB, UNZ, UNG, UNE, omission and truncation)
7:     UNECE. The segment specifications are in Annex B of the syntax rules; the
8:     general omission and truncation rules are in clauses 7.2 and 7.3. The text
9:     was prepared from the UNECE 1990 reprint (syntax version 2) and checked
10:     element by element against the UNECE syntax version 3 (1992) material on
11:     3 Nov 2026. Points that differ in version 3 are marked "(v3)".
12:   Parts 5 to 7 (CONTRL: UCI, S011, code lists 0083 and 0085)
13:     The CONTRL D.3 document hosted by ISO/TC 154/JWG 1.
14:   Parts 8 and 9 (service code lists 0035 and 0007)
15:     The service code lists hosted by ISO/TC 154/JWG 1.
16: 
17: 1. Interchange header UNB (UNECE, Annex B)
18: 
19:    Data elements in order (status M = mandatory, C = conditional):
20:      1  S001 SYNTAX IDENTIFIER                      M
21:           0001 Syntax identifier          a4   M  (e.g. UNOA, UNOB, UNOC)
22:           0002 Syntax version number      n1   M  (v3: 3 for the 1992 rules)
23:      2  S002 INTERCHANGE SENDER                     M
24:           0004 Sender identification      an..35 M
25:           0007 Partner identification code qualifier  an..4 C
26:           0008 Address for reverse routing an..14 C
27:      3  S003 INTERCHANGE RECIPIENT                  M
28:           0010 Recipient identification   an..35 M
29:           0007 Partner identification code qualifier  an..4 C
30:           0014 Routing address            an..14 C
31:      4  S004 DATE/TIME OF PREPARATION               M
32:           0017 Date                       n6   M  (YYMMDD)
33:           0019 Time                       n4   M  (HHMM)
34:      5  0020 INTERCHANGE CONTROL REFERENCE  an..14 M  (unique reference assigned by sender)
35:      6  S005 RECIPIENT'S REFERENCE/PASSWORD          C
36:           0022 Recipient's reference/password an..14 M
37:           0025 Recipient's reference/password qualifier an2 C
38:      7  0026 APPLICATION REFERENCE          an..14 C
39:      8  0029 PROCESSING PRIORITY CODE       a1     C
40:      9  0031 ACKNOWLEDGEMENT REQUEST        n1     C  (1 = acknowledgement requested)
41:     10  0032 COMMUNICATIONS AGREEMENT ID    an..35 C
42:     11  0035 TEST INDICATOR                 n1     C  (1 = the interchange is a test)
43: 
44: 2. Interchange trailer UNZ (UNECE, Annex B)
45: 
46:      1  0036 INTERCHANGE CONTROL COUNT      n..6   M
47:           The number of messages in the interchange or, if functional
48:           groups are used, the number of functional groups.
49:      2  0020 INTERCHANGE CONTROL REFERENCE  an..14 M
50:           Shall be identical to 0020 in UNB.
51: 
52: 3. Functional group header UNG and trailer UNE (UNECE, Annex B)
53: 
54:    UNG: 1 0038 Functional group identification; 2 S006 Application sender's
55:         identification (0040, 0007); 3 S007 Application recipient's
56:         identification (0044, 0007); 4 S004 Date/time of preparation;
57:         5 0048 Functional group reference number; 6 0051 Controlling agency;
58:         7 S008 Message version (0052, 0054, 0057); 8 0058 Application password
59:         (conditional).
60:    UNE: 1 0060 Number of messages in the group; 2 0048 Functional group
61:         reference number, identical to 0048 in UNG.
62: 
63: 4. Omission and truncation of data elements (UNECE, clauses 7.2 and 7.3)
64: 
65:    If a conditional data element is omitted and is followed by another data
66:    element, its position is indicated by retaining its data element separator.
67:    If one or more conditional data elements at the end of a segment are
68:    omitted, the segment may be truncated by the segment terminator; trailing
69:    data element separators are then not transmitted.

4: 
5:    o-------------------------------------------------------------------o
6:    |       SSID        Start Session                                   |
7:    |                                                                   |
8:    |       Start Session Phase     Initiator <---> Responder           |
9:    |-------------------------------------------------------------------|
10:    | Pos | Field     | Description                           | Format  |

14:    |   2 | SSIDCODE  | Initiator's Identification Code       | V X(25) |
15:    |  27 | SSIDPSWD  | Initiator's Password                  | V X(8)  |
16:    |  35 | SSIDSDEB  | Data Exchange Buffer Size             | V 9(5)  |
17:    |  40 | SSIDSR    | Send / Receive Capabilities (S/R/B)   | F X(1)  |
18:    |  41 | SSIDCMPR  | Buffer Compression Indicator (Y/N)    | F X(1)  |
19:    |  42 | SSIDREST  | Restart Indicator (Y/N)               | F X(1)  |
20:    |  43 | SSIDSPEC  | Special Logic Indicator (Y/N)         | F X(1)  |
21:    |  44 | SSIDCRED  | Credit                                | V 9(3)  |
22:    |  47 | SSIDAUTH  | Secure Authentication (Y/N)           | F X(1)  |
23:    |  48 | SSIDRSV1  | Reserved                              | F X(4)  |
24:    |  52 | SSIDUSER  | User Data                             | V X(8)  |
25:    |  60 | SSIDCR    | Carriage Return                       | F X(1)  |
26:    o-------------------------------------------------------------------o
27: 
28:       SSIDCMD   Command Code
29:       Character
30: 
31:       Value: 'X'  SSID Command identifier.
32: 
33:    SSIDLEV   Protocol Release Level                           Numeric(1)
34: 
35:              Used to specify the level of the ODETTE-FTP protocol
36: 
37:       Value: '1' for Revision 1.2
38:              '2' for Revision 1.3
39:              '4' for Revision 1.4
40:              '5' for Revision 2.0
41: 
42:              Future release levels will have higher numbers.  The
43:              protocol release level is negotiable, with the lowest level
44:              being selected.
45: 
46:              Note: ODETTE File Transfer Protocol 1.3 (RFC 2204)
47:                    specifies '1' for the release level, despite adhering
48:                    to revision 1.3.
49: 
50:    SSIDCODE  Initiator's Identification Code                  String(25)
51: 
52:     Format:  See Identification Code (Section 5.4)
53: 
54:              Uniquely identifies the Initiator (sender) participating in
55:              the ODETTE-FTP session.
56: 
57:              It is an application implementation issue to link the
58:              expected [X.509] certificate to the SSIDCODE provided.
59: 
60:    SSIDPSWD  Initiator's Password                              String(8)
61: 
62:              Key to authenticate the sender.  Assigned by bilateral
63:              agreement.
64: 
65:    SSIDSDEB  Data Exchange Buffer Size                        Numeric(5)
66: 
67:     Minimum: 128
68:     Maximum: 99999
69: 
70:              The length, in octets, of the largest Data Exchange Buffer
71:              that can be accepted by the location.  The length includes
72:              the command octet but does not include the Stream
73:              Transmission Header.
74: 
75:              After negotiation, the smallest size will be selected.
76: 
77:    SSIDSR    Send / Receive Capabilities                       Character
78: 
79:       Value: 'S'  Location can only send files.
80:              'R'  Location can only receive files.
81:              'B'  Location can both send and receive files.
82: 
83:              Sending and receiving will be serialised during the
84:              session, so parallel transmissions will not take place in
85:              the same session.
86: 
87:              An error occurs if adjacent locations both specify the send
88:              or receive capability.
89: 
90:    SSIDCMPR  Buffer Compression Indicator                      Character
91: 
92:       Value: 'Y'  The location can handle OFTP data buffer compression
93:              'N'  The location cannot handle OFTP buffer compression
94: 
95:              Compression is only used if supported by both locations.
96: 
97:              The compression mechanism referred to here applies to each
98:              individual OFTP data buffer.  This is different from the
99:              file compression mechanism in OFTP, which involves the
100:              compression of whole files.
101: 
102:    SSIDREST  Restart Indicator                                 Character
103: 
104:       Value: 'Y'  The location can handle the restart of a partially
105:                   transmitted file.
106:              'N'  The location cannot restart a file.
107: 
108:    SSIDSPEC  Special Logic Indicator                           Character
109: 
110:       Value: 'Y'  Location can handle Special Logic
111:              'N'  Location cannot handle Special Logic
112: 
113:              Special Logic is only used if supported by both locations.
114: 
115:              The Special Logic extensions are only useful to access an
116:              X.25 network via an asynchronous entry and are not
117:              supported for TCP/IP connections.
118: 
119:    SSIDCRED  Credit                                           Numeric(3)
120: 
121:     Maximum: 999
122: 
123:              The number of consecutive Data Exchange Buffers sent by the
124:              Speaker before it must wait for a Credit (CDT) command from
125:              the Listener.
126: 
127:              The credit value is only applied to Data flow in the Data
128:              Transfer phase.
129: 
130:              The Speaker's available credit is initialised to SSIDCRED
131:              when it receives a Start File Positive Answer (SFPA)
132:              command from the Listener.  It is zeroed by the End File
133:              (EFID) command.
134: 
135:              After negotiation, the smallest size must be selected in
136:              the answer of the Responder, otherwise a protocol error
137:              will abort the session.
138: 
139:              Negotiation of the "credit-window-size" parameter.
140: 
141:              Window Size m  -- SSID ------------>
142:                             <------------ SSID --  Window Size n
143:                                                   (n less than or
144:                                                    equal to m)
145:              Note: negotiated value will be "n".
146: 
147:    SSIDAUTH  Secure Authentication                             Character
148: 
149:       Value: 'Y'  The location requires secure authentication.  'N'  The
150:              location does not require secure authentication.
151: 
152:              Secure authentication is only used if agreed by both
153:              locations.
154: 
155:              If the answer of the Responder does not match with the
156:              authentication requirements of the Initiator, then the
157:              Initiator must abort the session.
158: 
159:              No negotiation of authentication is allowed.
160: 
161:              authentication p  -- SSID ------------>
162:                                <------------ SSID --  authentication q
163: 
164:              p == q -> continue.
165:              p != q -> abort.
166: 
167:    SSIDRSV1  Reserved                                          String(4)
168: 
169:              This field is reserved for future use.
170: 
171:    SSIDUSER  User Data                                         String(8)
172: 
173:              May be used by ODETTE-FTP in any way.  If unused, it should
174:              be initialised to spaces.  It is expected that a bilateral
175:              agreement exists as to the meaning of the data.
176: 
177:    SSIDCR    Carriage Return                                   Character
178: 
179:       Value: Character with hex value '0D' or '8D'.
